key_insight: IMCBench shows that multimodal medical LLMs can describe images well yet still vary substantially in safety, accuracy, and uncertainty handling during realistic multi-turn clinical conversations.
clinical_relevance: This benchmark highlights the need to evaluate medical AI on conversation-level safety, not just image recognition or single-turn question answering, before considering decision support or triage use.
method: Built image-grounded, multi-turn medical conversations using real public clinical images plus synthetic patient profiles.
Scored eight frontier multimodal models across safety, accuracy, and uncertainty using 1–5 LLM-as-Jury ratings calibrated to clinician annotations.
Compared four model families and ran ablations removing visual input or EHR context to test what improves safe guidance.
evidence_signal: Claude Opus 4.6 ranked highest overall at 3.61, with safety declining for malignant and rare cases (Δ = -0.27 each) and dropping when visual input or EHR context was removed.
watch_item: Because the benchmark relies on synthetic profiles and LLM-as-Jury scoring, results may not fully capture real-world clinical risk, workflow constraints, or patient diversity.
paper_title: IMCBench: A benchmark for multimodal LLMs in Image-grounded Medical Conversations
